name: PT Indofarma Tbk

frontmatter.title: Indofarma: a zero equity behind a frozen share price
frontmatter.summary: Indofarma now earns a positive gross margin on its H1-2026 run-rate, but net debt exceeds any enterprise value the operating business can support. The equity is worth nothing on the abandonment, perpetuity and liquidation tests alike. We keep SELL with a zero target; the last quote is a stale pre-suspension print, not a price.
thesis: The H1-2026 pack shows gross margin at 10.0% and EBITDA near breakeven, so the collapse is now a balance-sheet problem, not only an operating one.
Net debt of IDR694.6bn on the last audited balance sheet exceeds a DCF enterprise value that is at best zero once the negative perpetuity is floored at abandonment.
The IDR629.7bn of shareholder loans is senior to the shares, secured on land and buildings, and matures within a year; the state, not the market, decides whether it is rolled or converted.
The shares have been suspended since July 2024 and did not trade in 2025; the quoted price is the last print, so any upside to it is arithmetic on a fiction.

The FY2024 accounts were qualified and the state auditor found indicated criminal irregularities in the financial management of the years through 2023; the house screen classes this as a manipulation-class governance flag.

catalysts.event: FY2026 outlook commentary from the new board and any statement on state capital injection
Audited FY2026 financial statements, the first full post-homologation year
BEI review of the trading suspension; delisting is not automatic but remains a live risk

blocks.text: **SELL, target Rp0, last price Rp126.** The target is a fundamental value of zero for the equity, not a forecast of where the shares will print: the stock has been suspended by the exchange since 2 July 2024 and recorded no trading volume in any quarter of 2025 [S4][S5]. The mechanical total return of -100.0% is therefore a statement about the balance sheet, not about a trade anyone can execute.

The company is PT Indofarma Tbk, a Bekasi-based manufacturer of generic prescription drugs, over-the-counter medicines and, historically, medical devices, controlled by the state through PT Bio Farma [S0][S4]. It is the weakest listed entity in the Indonesian pharmaceutical holding structure. FY2025 net sales were IDR151.6bn, cost of goods sold exceeded revenue, and equity at the year-end was IDR-706.9bn, a deficiency larger than the whole asset base of IDR536.0bn [S4]. It survives on shareholder loans now totalling IDR629.7bn [S4].

What changed in this revision is the operating base, and it changed in the company's favour. The H1-2026 pack shows the first positive gross margin in five years, at 10.0%, with EBIT still negative but EBITDA near breakeven after the workforce cut to 51.0 employees [S0][S4]. The prior draft carried a negative gross margin and treated the gross line as permanently negative. That was a drift defect and it is corrected: FY2026E is rebuilt from the H1-2026 run-rate, with gross margin held at the last actual and opex at the H1 ratio, which produces EBITDA of IDR1.6bn for FY2026E rather than a deepening loss [S0]. The equity is still worth zero, but for the honest reason: net debt of IDR694.6bn is larger than any enterprise value this business supports, not because the gross line never turns.

The variant view is not that the business is bad; the filings make that plain. The variant view is that **the quoted price is not a price**. Because no shares have changed hands for more than two years, the last print of Rp126 still capitalises the company at IDR390.5bn while the balance sheet shows negative net worth. Any holder marking the position at that price is marking an asset the market has refused to trade.

What moves the value is narrowly defined. First, whether Bio Farma routes enough contract manufacturing and government-tender volume through the Bekasi plant to hold the H1 gross margin [S4]. Second, whether the state injects capital or converts its loans into equity — either repairs solvency but dilutes the listed minority; the June 2026 report that management is coordinating a Danantara injection is not in the registry and has no published terms, so we do not value it [S2]. Third, whether BEI resumes trading or delists the shares [S5].

Indofarma manufactures and sells pharmaceutical products in Indonesia and, historically, abroad. The data pack describes three reporting activities — medicines, medical devices and other products, and pharmaceutical engineering — and notes that the company also markets and distributes medicines and medical devices and operates a clinical laboratory [S0]. The commercial reality after the restructuring is narrower. The company's own annual report shows pharmaceutical production of 126 mn units in FY2025, down from 164 mn units in FY2024, with 149 NIE marketing authorisations in force at the end of the year [S4]. Medical-device output fell to nil, from a small base, over the same period [S4].

The customer base is the Indonesian public health system and the trade. Indofarma's historical franchise was built on government procurement — generic medicines supplied to public hospitals and puskesmas through the e-catalogue — plus branded OTC products such as OBH syrup and Indomag [S4]. That mix is structurally low-margin: tender prices are set by the state buyer, and the company competes against far larger generic manufacturers with better plant utilisation. The annual report itself attributes the FY2025 production cut to limited working capital rather than to demand [S4], which tells you the constraint is cash, not market access.

The strategy now is explicit and modest. Management describes a shift to a demand-driven operating model, selective plant operation, and toll manufacturing for other parties plus natural-extract processing, in order to raise capacity utilisation without carrying inventory risk [S4]. The 2026 plan presented at the December 2025 public expose targeted revenue growth of more than a hundred percent against the FY2025 prognosis, on a rebalanced portfolio weighted to pharmaceutical products [S2]. In October 2026 the company signed a memorandum of understanding with the Danantara development fund, Institut Teknologi Bandung and a technology partner to explore downstreaming of medicinal-plant research; it is an exploration agreement with no volume, price or revenue commitment, and we do not treat it as a commercial contract [S8]. None of this is yet visible in the numbers.

The footprint is a single large manufacturing site at Jl. Indofarma No. 1 in Bekasi, west Java, built for a volume the company no longer has [S0][S4]. The most telling operating statistic in the annual report is the workforce: headcount fell from over four hundred to 51.0 employees during the restructuring, a cut management describes as executed without disruption [S4]. A plant of that scale run by that many people is a plant running well below any sensible utilisation.

Group and control matter more here than in a normal industrial. Indofarma is a state-owned enterprise within the pharmaceutical holding led by PT Bio Farma, which the data pack identifies as its parent [S0]. The state's economic interest is overwhelming and the free float is minimal [S0]. Control sits with the Ministry of State-Owned Enterprises and, since the creation of the Danantara sovereign fund structure, with that layer of the state apparatus as well; the 2025 shareholder meeting amended the articles to conform to the revised state-enterprise law [S2]. For a minority holder this means every consequential decision — recapitalisation, asset transfer, debt conversion, delisting — is taken by the controlling shareholder, not by the market.

Two structural facts complete the picture. The distribution subsidiary PT Indofarma Global Medika was declared bankrupt and has been deconsolidated, which is why trade payables fell to IDR17.4bn from a multiple of that level in a single year [S4]. And the company emerged from a suspension-of-debt-payment process with a homologated composition plan that became final and binding in March 2025, following a Supreme Court cassation ruling [S4]. In plain terms, this is a company that has already been through insolvency-adjacent proceedings once and is now executing the settlement obligations that came out of them.

Indonesian pharmaceuticals is a large, slow-growing, price-regulated market. Demand is driven by population, the national health-insurance scheme, and the state's procurement budget; supply is fragmented across multinational subsidiaries, large domestic groups and a long tail of generic manufacturers [S0][S4]. There is no populated PHARMA industry driver deck behind this name: the only reviewed deck in the registry is the macro deck, which carries Indonesian CPI and real GDP growth in a mid-single-digit range for FY2027E, so nominal industry growth at that level is the reasonable backdrop and no industry-specific volume or price series is claimed [S0][S7].

Within that market Indofarma is a challenger with a shrinking share. Its FY2025 revenue of IDR151.6bn is small against the listed peer set — Kalbe, Kimia Farma, Darya-Varia, Merck, Phapros and Pyridam all compete for the same tender and prescription pools [S4]. The company's own disclosure that 149 NIE authorisations remain in force shows the product portfolio survives; what has collapsed is the ability to manufacture and sell at volume [S4]. In a tender market, the loss of working capital is self-reinforcing: you cannot bid for volume without inventory, and you cannot build inventory without cash.

The regulatory framework cuts both ways. BPOM registration and halal certification are barriers to entry that protect incumbents' authorisations, and local-content rules favour domestic manufacturers in government procurement [S4]. But price ceilings transfer most of the benefit of that protection to the state buyer, and the state-pharma holding structure explicitly coordinates the portfolios of Bio Farma, Kimia Farma and Indofarma to avoid duplication [S4]. Indofarma's assigned role in that division of labour has been medical devices and herbal or natural-extract products, which is precisely the segment where its output has gone to zero [S4]. Being the designated specialist in a segment you cannot fund is not a moat; it is a trap.

Five-forces assessment, briefly. Buyer power is very high: the government is the dominant purchaser and sets prices through the catalogue [S4]. Supplier power is moderate: active pharmaceutical ingredients are imported and priced in dollars, which is why management cited rupiah weakness as a margin threat in June 2026 [S7]. Competitive rivalry is intense and consolidating around larger, better-capitalised groups [S4]. Threat of new entrants is low at the regulatory level but irrelevant, because the incumbents are capacity-rich and Indofarma is the one with idle plant. Substitutes are real: imported generics and, increasingly, contract-manufactured products from better-run plants [S4].

The moat verdict is none. Indofarma has authorisations, a plant and a brand heritage, and no mechanism — no network effect, no switching cost, no distribution density that its competitors lack, no pricing power — that lets it earn above its cost of capital [S4]. The evidence that any moat was widening would be gross margin turning positive and holding; the filings show negative gross margin in each of the last four audited years, and the positive H1-2026 margin is a single half-year, not yet a trend [S4][S0].

External influences to monitor are the rupiah (imported input costs), the state budget for procurement, health-sector regulation on tenders and halal rules, and the government's willingness to keep funding a loss-making subsidiary [S4][S7]. The last of these is the only one that decides the equity value.

The five-year record is one of collapse followed by stabilisation at a very low level. Revenue fell from IDR980.4bn in FY2022 to IDR523.6bn, then IDR210.4bn, then IDR151.6bn [S4]. Cost of goods sold exceeded revenue in each of the last four audited years, so gross profit was negative, at IDR-19.2bn in FY2025 [S4].

The reported operating result needs restating before it is used. The LK's operating line is struck after IDR80.1bn of one-off other income from the debt settlement, so the loss it prints understates the operating loss. On a gross basis the FY2025 operating loss is IDR-121.5bn and FY2024's is IDR-268.4bn, which we key into the model as history [S4]. The data pack's FY2025 figure of IDR-121.5bn is a third, non-comparable basis: it neither matches the LK's reported line nor the gross line, and we do not use it. Total operating expense on the same gross basis was IDR102.3bn in FY2025 and IDR230.8bn in FY2024, being selling plus general and administrative costs [S4]. Net loss attributable to shareholders was IDR-78.0bn [S4].

The single most important correction to the data pack is depreciation. The pack carries FY2025 D&A of about a twelfth of the charge the accounts actually bear. The audited notes show factory depreciation of IDR12.1bn charged into cost of goods sold in FY2025, plus further depreciation in selling and administrative expense and amortisation of intangibles [S4]. We restate D&A on the LK basis, which rebuilds EBITDA rather than the flattering figure the pack implies. A cash-cost or EBITDA-based argument for this company built on the pack would be wrong by an order of magnitude in the add-back, and we do not make one.

Cash generation is the core problem. FY2025 operating cash flow was IDR-210.0bn, after cash paid to suppliers and employees dwarfed receipts from customers [S4]. Financing activities provided a positive inflow of similar scale in the same year [S4]. In other words the business did not fund itself; the shareholder did. Cash at the year-end was IDR5.7bn [S4], and the June 2026 balance sheet shows it lower still.

The balance sheet is the reason the equity is worth nothing. Total assets were IDR536.0bn against liabilities that exceed them, leaving equity of IDR-706.9bn [S4]. Debt on the last audited balance sheet is IDR700.3bn, of which shareholder loans are IDR629.7bn across the short- and long-term tranches — the short-term portion maturing in September 2026 is IDR245.3bn — plus a long-term bank loan; cash is IDR5.7bn, so net debt is IDR694.6bn on the audited balance sheet at 31 December 2025, the same date used in the valuation bridge [S4]. Every rupiah of that stack ranks ahead of the 3,099 mn shares. A liquidation of the plant at its book value of IDR336.6bn would not reach the creditors, let alone the shareholders. The FY2025 improvement in equity from the prior year's deeper deficiency is largely a deconsolidation effect from the bankrupt distribution subsidiary and the debt-restructuring gain, not an earnings recovery [S4].

Our forecasts are rebuilt from the last actual, which is now the H1-2026 pack rather than the FY2025 LK. The first half annualises to revenue of IDR158.1bn, 4.3% above FY2025, and growth then settles at 5.0% a year before easing to IDR188.5bn by FY2030E [S0][S4]. We do not adopt the more-than-doubling target management presented for 2026 [S2]: it requires working capital the company does not have, and the FY2025 production cut was itself blamed on working-capital limits [S4].

Gross margin is held at the H1-2026 actual of 10.0% in every forecast year and in the terminal value. It is the only positive gross margin in five years, produced after the headcount cut and the shift to selective plant operation and toll manufacturing, and the base case must reproduce it rather than extrapolate the FY2025 loss [S0][S4]. Opex is held at 17.0% of sales, the H1-2026 ratio, rather than reverting to the pre-restructuring cost base [S0]. Working capital is held at 44.0% of revenue, the trade-working-capital ratio the LK balances give at end-2025 on the same definition the forecast uses [S4].

The result is EBIT of IDR-11.1bn in FY2026E and IDR-13.2bn in FY2030E. The operating line stays negative because a 10.0% gross margin does not cover a 17.0% expense ratio, but EBITDA is positive at IDR1.6bn in FY2026E and IDR-1.9bn in FY2030E. That is a stabilised, cash-generative-at-the-EBITDA-line business that still cannot service its interest bill — a different and less dramatic finding than the prior draft's permanently negative gross line [S0].

Capex is held at maintenance level, 0.5% of sales, because there is neither cash nor a growth project to fund [S4]. No dividend is assumed; the company has a capital deficiency and has paid nothing in the price history [S4][S0]. We assume no new shares in the base case: the share count has been unchanged at 3,099 mn shares through the restructuring [S4], though a recapitalisation would change that.

Earnings-quality flags, per the house screen. The Sloan ratio is not a useful lens on a company whose net loss exceeds its equity, so we use the cash-conversion test instead: the operating cash outflow of IDR-210.0bn exceeded the net loss, meaning the accounting loss understates the cash burn. That is the reverse of the usual manipulation pattern and equally disqualifying [S4]. On divergence flags, receivables fell with revenue rather than outgrowing it, while inventory rose on a falling sales base [S4]: inventory days have ballooned, which is either a tender build or unsaleable stock, and we classify it as an unresolved optics-class divergence rather than a finding. Related-party gravity is high and structural: the controlling shareholder is the lender of IDR629.7bn, of which IDR245.3bn is short-term, the parent group is a principal customer through the holding's portfolio allocation, and the state sets tender prices [S4]. The IDX regime flag is dominant: the shares have been suspended since 2 July 2024 and remain on the exchange's suspension list, so the name fails the investability gate before any fundamental work begins [S5][S6]. Two governance findings are classified under governance below: a state audit finding covering the years through 2023, which we treat as manipulation-class until the criminal process resolves, and the FY2024 qualified opinion, which we treat as optics-class because the audited FY2024 filing could not be extracted to identify its basis [S4][S9].

Capital allocation has been defensive in the extreme: asset sales of non-collateralised assets, headcount cuts, selective plant operation, and reliance on shareholder funding [S4]. The claims stack ahead of the equity is the operative fact. Shareholder loans total IDR629.7bn; the IDR245.3bn short-term portion matures in September 2026 and the facilities are secured on land and buildings; the workforce left under a joint agreement with the labour union that set an early-retirement programme, and the severance was paid in cash as a post-homologation legal obligation [S4]. Any conversion of that senior loan into equity would issue 4,998 mn shares new shares against the existing 3,099 mn shares — a dilution larger than the current share count itself — which sizes the dilution but does not value a recapitalisation that has no agreed terms [S4]. There is no growth capital, no buyback and no dividend. The only allocation decision that matters now is how the state chooses to convert its support into capital.

The method set is dictated by the facts. P/E and dividend yield are undefined: the company makes a net loss and pays nothing. EV/EBITDA is arithmetically available on FY2026E EBITDA of IDR1.6bn, but at that level a multiple is a rounding error against net debt of IDR694.6bn — the enterprise value implied by any peer multiple on this EBITDA is smaller than one year's interest charge. We therefore value the operating business by discounted cash flow, weighted between two constructions of the same forecast, and use the balance sheet as a liquidation cross-check rather than a method.

The cost of capital build gives a cost of equity of 17.9% and a WACC of 11.1% [S0][S4]. The WACC is inside the house band for Indonesian rupiah names: we set the unlevered beta a notch above the PHARMA template default, on the argument that a negative-equity, post-homologation manufacturer carries more systematic risk than the sector median regression, and that lifts the computed rate to the lower edge of the band [S4]. The capital structure is debt-heavy by book value because equity is negative, so the debt weight pulls the blend down; on a company that cannot service its debt from operations, that weight is not cheap funding but a symptom. The relevant rate for the equity claim is the cost of equity of 17.9%, and discounting at that rate makes the present value lower still. At either rate the equity is zero.

We run two constructions of the same forecast and weight them. The life DCF, which stops at the year that maximises cumulative present value, produces an enterprise value of IDR0.0bn: the forecast never earns its cost of capital, so the best outcome is to stop, and the engine floors the result at abandonment rather than carrying loss years to infinity. The perpetuity DCF produces IDR-72.9bn, with a negative terminal value, because on these margins the business earns less than its cost of capital in perpetuity [S4]. We weight the life construction at seven tenths and the perpetuity at three tenths; net debt of IDR694.6bn exceeds either enterprise value. Equity is floored at zero for limited liability, which gives Rp0 per share. We do not add the listing shell or the state's implicit support to reach a positive number, because neither is a contractual claim available to minority holders.

Cross-checks, and why they diverge. The liquidation check is the strongest of them: property, plant and equipment at book value is IDR336.6bn against net debt of IDR694.6bn, and the shareholder loans are secured on land and buildings [S4]. Even a buyer paying book value for the plant leaves the creditors short and nothing for the shares; a distressed sale would be worse. An EV/sales cross-check at peer multiples would produce a positive enterprise value and is the wrong tool: applying a revenue multiple to a manufacturer earning a 10.0% gross margin assumes a buyer who can fix the cost base, and any such buyer would deal with the creditors and the lender-shareholder, not with the listed minority. A price-to-book check is unavailable because book value is negative. Every method that respects the capital structure returns zero; the only methods that return more ignore it.

What today's price implies is the crux. At Rp126 the last pre-suspension print capitalises the company at IDR390.5bn, a positive number on a balance sheet with negative equity [S0][S4]. Add net debt of IDR694.6bn — both figures are from the last audited balance sheet at 31 December 2025, so the bridge is a year old and the June-2026 net debt is higher, which only strengthens the conclusion — and the implied enterprise value is the whole of that claim. A reverse DCF on our WACC of 11.13% and terminal growth of 4.0% says a business with that enterprise value would have to earn perpetual EBITDA of IDR74.4bn, which is the implied enterprise value multiplied by the WACC minus terminal growth and divided by one plus terminal growth; that is roughly half its own FY2025 revenue, with no year in the LK or the H1-2026 pack anywhere near it [S4]. The alternative reading of the price is a state transfer large enough to make the existing equity whole; that would be a transfer to minorities that no controlling shareholder has signalled [S4][S2]. Neither is a base case.

Sensitivity is dominated by one threshold rather than a slope. EBIT turns positive only when the gross margin exceeds the 17.0% expense ratio, so moving gross margin a point either side of the H1-2026 actual leaves the operating loss in place and the equity at zero [S0]. The discount rate matters less than usual: cash flow is negative in the near years and the life construction is floored at abandonment, so raising or lowering WACC changes the size of a negative number, not its sign.

The multiple-survival test does not apply in its usual form, but its logic does: a buyer would pay a positive multiple only of the EBITDA that survives as cash to the equity, and here EBITDA of IDR1.6bn is smaller than the interest charge on debt that ranks ahead of the shares. That is the whole valuation.

Downside risks, with likelihood and impact. **Liquidity and delisting (high likelihood, certain impact):** the shares have been suspended since 2 July 2024, and while BEI has stated that delisting is not automatic [S5], a continued failure to meet reporting or free-float obligations keeps the suspension alive and the position untradeable [S6]. **Solvency (high, severe):** equity is negative by more than the asset base, net debt is IDR694.6bn, and the shareholder loans of IDR629.7bn are secured, so continued existence depends on funding that can be withdrawn [S4]. **Operating (medium, high):** the positive H1-2026 gross margin is a single half-year and still does not cover the expense ratio, so the operating line stays negative on the run-rate [S0]. **Working capital and input costs (medium, high):** imported active ingredients are priced in dollars, which exposes the gross line to rupiah weakness, a risk management itself flagged in June 2026 [S7]. **Governance and related-party (high, high):** the controlling shareholder is also the secured lender, in part the customer, and the party that would set the terms of any recapitalisation; any conversion of the senior loan would issue more shares than exist today, and minority holders have no say [S4]. A state audit produced an investigative finding of irregularities in the financial management of the years through 2023, now with the Attorney General [S9]. **Regulatory and policy (medium, medium):** tender prices, halal rules and the state's holding-company portfolio decisions can move volume without notice [S4]. **Reporting (medium, medium):** the FY2024 accounts carry a qualified opinion, the shares are suspended over disclosure history, and the auditor is not a Big Four practice [S4][S5].

The upside risks are real but narrow. A directed state capital injection would repair the balance sheet; a June 2026 press report says management is coordinating one with Danantara, but no terms are published and we could not archive the underlying article, so it is an upside risk and not value [S7]. The question for a minority holder in any injection is the price at which it is done, given that the senior loan would rank ahead of, or convert in front of, the listed shares [S4]. A large contract-manufacturing award from within the Bio Farma group would lift utilisation quickly [S4]. Resumption of trading would restore a market price, which could exceed a fundamental view if retail demand for a low-priced state name re-emerges [S5]. We give these weight in the bull case and none in the base case.

The scenarios shock the same two drivers by mirrored amounts — revenue growth and gross margin, five points and three points each way — so neither side is a stacked case; the base carries the larger weight at one in two, with three in ten to the bear and one in five to the bull. The value is zero in all three, because the equity is out of the money against net debt of IDR694.6bn in every scenario we can source, including the bull case's higher margin, which raises EBITDA without ever reaching the debt stack [S4]. The bear case — funding stops and the company re-enters a debt-payment suspension — is the one that ends in delisting or a wipe-out. The bull case requires a state decision, not a business outcome, and even then the arithmetic favours the creditor-shareholder over the minority.

Signposts that would change our view: a signed, quantified recapitalisation at terms that leave existing shares with positive value; gross margin exceeding the expense ratio for two consecutive quarters; published contract-manufacturing volumes with named counterparties; resumed trading with audited interim accounts; a resolution of the state audit and Attorney General case without further findings [S9]; and any disclosure that the shareholder loan has been converted at a premium to market. Absent those, the view holds.

Ownership and control are concentrated in the Indonesian state through the Bio Farma pharmaceutical holding, with a free float in the low single digits [S0]. This is the governance fact that subsumes all others: the same ultimate shareholder appoints the board, sets strategy, provides the loan that keeps the company alive, and would determine the terms of any capital injection. Related-party flows are therefore not an exception but the operating model — shareholder loans of IDR629.7bn, secured on land and buildings, are the clearest example [S4].

The audit trail is the part a minority holder should read first. The FY2024 accounts carry a qualified opinion and an emphasis-of-matter paragraph [S4]; the FY2025 accounts carry an unqualified opinion from KAP Heliantono dan Rekan, a non-Big-Four practice [S4]. Separately, the state audit agency completed an investigative audit of the company's financial management of the period through 2023 and referred findings indicating irregularities, with an indication of state loss, to the Attorney General in May 2024 [S9]. We classify that finding as manipulation-class until the criminal process resolves — one confirmed finding of that kind is an automatic pass on the name under the house screen — while the FY2024 qualification is optics-class because the audited FY2024 filing is a scanned document that could not be extracted, so we cannot identify its basis, and we say so rather than infer one [S4].

The IDX regime flags are material. The shares have been suspended since 2 July 2024 and remain on the exchange's suspension list [S5][S6]; the free float is below the exchange's minimum threshold [S0]. Under the house earnings-quality screen the suspension is the gate that matters: a negative-equity issuer whose shares cannot be traded is not investable on the long side regardless of the fundamental story, and the correct action is to log it rather than to haircut estimates around it.

ESG exposures are mostly inherited rather than managed. Pharmaceutical manufacturing carries effluent and waste-handling obligations at the Bekasi plant; product quality and halal certification are the licence-to-operate issues; and the social dimension is dominated by the treatment of the workforce through the restructuring, which the annual report presents as orderly and governed by a joint agreement with the labour union [S4]. On governance the score is poor: a company that needed a homologated debt settlement, carries a qualified prior-year opinion and a live state-audit referral, and is majority-owned by a shareholder that is also its secured lender offers minority holders almost no protection. Pledged shares, serial rights issues and beneficial-ownership opacity are not disclosed as issues in the filings we archived, and we record that as "checked, none found" rather than as a clean bill of health [S4].

The dated catalysts are few because the company is not trading and has no dividend. The next hard information event is the audited FY2026 report, the first full post-homologation year, which will show whether the first-half revenue run-rate — our full-year estimate is IDR158.1bn — survives the second half [S0][S4]. Before that, any statement from the board or the shareholder on a capital injection or on the 2026 work plan is the event that would reprice the name, and it is not scheduled [S7]. BEI's periodic review of the suspension is the third: it does not automatically end in delisting [S5], but it is the mechanism by which the position either becomes tradeable or dies. The state audit referral to the Attorney General is the fourth, with no court timetable we can source [S9].

Between events we monitor four things. Production volume in million units, the cleanest read on whether the plant is coming back [S4]. Gross margin against the expense ratio, which must clear it for two consecutive quarters before the operating line turns and the thesis is wrong. Cash and the shareholder-loan balance, which together are the company's oxygen supply. And the working-capital triangle of receivables, inventory and payables, where the inventory build on falling sales is the one line that could be either recovery or rot [S4]. We will refresh after the FY2026 accounts or on any announcement touching capital structure, whichever comes first.

valuation.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

bear.narrative: Working capital runs out before volume recovers, the shareholder stops funding, the maturity of the Rp255.7bn short-term facilities is not rolled, and the company re-enters a PKPU; the equity is wiped or the shares are delisted.

bull.narrative: Bio Farma routes contract manufacturing and government tenders through the Bekasi plant and gross margin rises 3pp above the H1 level; the shares relist. A Danantara capital injection is reported to be under discussion but no terms are agreed or published, so it is not valued: any conversion of the Rp629.7bn senior shareholder loan would issue shares ahead of the minority.

sensitivity.title: DCF value per share vs WACC and terminal growth
12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

football.label: DCF to end of life (no terminal value)

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: H1-2026 revenue of Rp79.0bn, annualised, is Rp158.1bn, +4.3% on FY2025 net sales of Rp151.6bn [S0]. That is the only post-restructuring run-rate in the pack and the base we adopt; the 112% revenue target in the company's 2026 plan is not achievable on the working capital the LK shows [S2][S4].

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: H1-2026 gross profit was Rp7.9bn on Rp79.0bn of sales, a 10.0% gross margin, after the headcount cut to 51 and the shift to selective plant operation and toll manufacturing [S0][S4]. We hold the last actual at 10% through the window: it is the only positive gross margin in five years and the base case must reproduce it, not the FY2025 loss [S0].

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: H1-2026 operating expense was Rp13.3bn on Rp79.0bn of revenue, 16.8% of sales, against Rp102.3bn (67.5%) for FY2025 after the 413-to-51 workforce cut [S0][S4]. We hold the H1 run-rate at 17% rather than reverting to the pre-restructuring cost base.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated from the LK note, not the data pack: factory depreciation alone was Rp12.07bn in FY2025 and Rp12.35bn in FY2024, versus the Rp1.1bn the pack carries [S4]. As revenue grows the fixed charge falls as a percentage of sales.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: Capex was Rp0.4bn in FY2025 and Rp4.7bn in FY2023; the plant is idle capacity, not a growth asset, and there is no cash to invest. We allow only maintenance-level spend at 0.5% of sales [S4].

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: Restated to the forecast definition on the LK balances: trade receivables Rp18.7bn plus inventories Rp65.6bn less trade payables Rp17.4bn is Rp66.9bn at end-2025, 44.1% of FY2025 revenue [S4]. Holding 44% keeps the forecast on one definition with the history and removes the data pack's all-current-liabilities line.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: Loss-making with a deferred-tax asset that the AR writes against earnings; no cash tax is expected in the forecast window, so 0% is the honest rate rather than the statutory 22% [S4].

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: H1-2026 interest expense of Rp27.4bn on about Rp713bn of average debt annualises to 7.7% [S0], consistent with the 7% contractual rate on the Rp255.7bn short-term Bio Farma facilities and the 6.9% Type E rate in note 26 [S4]. We use 7.7%, replacing the 4.5% carried from the FY2025 average; it is mid-peer in PHARMA.

assumptions.label: Interest income on cash
assumptions.basis: Cash was Rp5.7bn at end-2025 and Rp4.4bn at 30 June 2026, immaterial to earnings [S4][S0].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: The Rp255.7bn short-term Bio Farma facilities mature in September 2026 and the Rp220.2bn tranche funded the post-homologation employee obligations [S4]; the shareholder has funded the operating deficit every year, so the base case rolls the facilities and adds Rp70bn a year, roughly the modelled cash deficit, rather than assuming funding stops. Funding stopping is the bear case, not the base.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating income
assumptions.basis: FY2025 other income of Rp80.1bn was a one-off loan-restructuring gain; we do not repeat it [S4].

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: Minorities were -Rp0.02bn after the deconsolidation of the bankrupt distribution subsidiary IGM; treated as nil [S4].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: No dividend has been paid in the price history and the company carries a capital deficiency of Rp706.9bn; payout stays at zero [S4].

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Shares have been unchanged at 3,099,267,500 through the restructuring [S4]. A state recapitalisation or debt-to-equity conversion is a live possibility but is not our base case, and it would dilute rather than add value to existing holders.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: 4% aligns with the 4.0-4.5% common PHARMA peer terminal rate and with the 4% long-run revenue growth in this model, below the house long-run nominal GDP assumption for Indonesia (5.29%), because this is a stabilised generic manufacturer, not a franchise compounding with the economy.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E is set about 20pp below the last actual on both drivers. The model has gross margin -10.0%, opex 62% of sales, EBIT -Rp118.9bn and net loss -Rp150.5bn. The S0 quarterly pack you use for the H1 revenue claim shows H1-2026 revenue Rp79.0bn, gross profit +Rp7.9bn (+10.0% margin), EBIT -Rp5.4bn and net loss -Rp33.1bn; your FY2026E therefore implies an H2 net loss of -Rp117bn, 3.5x H1, and a 20pp gross-margin reversal with no source. Section 3 states gross margin never reaches positive territory in our window, which the same series contradicts. The rating survives because net debt is Rp718.4bn, but the base case misses the most-likely standard.
challenges.answer: FY2026E rebuilt from the H1-2026 pack: revenue annualises to 158.1 (+4.3%), gross margin held at the H1 actual 10.0%, opex at the H1 ratio 17.0%, H2 assumed flat on H1; EBIT -11.1, EBITDA +1.6, net loss -65.0 against H1 -33.1. The never-positive sentence is deleted. Rating unchanged because net debt 694.6 exceeds any EV [S0][S4].

challenges.challenge: The FY2025A base year still uses the data pack EBIT of -Rp208.2bn (implied opex Rp189.0bn) even though F5 restates opex to Rp94.857bn and the AR income statement (S4 p16) shows an operating loss of -Rp41.484bn reported and -Rp121.6bn excluding the +Rp80.066bn other income. No ebit fact was added, so the engine keeps pack:ebit and the 65.4pp calibration gap is created inside the model. Section 3 claims the underlying operating loss is roughly double what the pack shows, which is inverted: -Rp121.6bn is 0.58x the pack -Rp208.2bn. The restated opex fact also stops at G&A and omits selling expense (~Rp7.5bn).
challenges.answer: Added ebit facts FY2025A -121.549 (F22, anchored on the LK -41.484 and adjusted for the +80.066 other income) and FY2024A -268.353 (F24), plus total selling plus G&A opex 102.333 (F5) and 230.845 (F23). The engine now uses fact:ebit and the calibration gap collapses. Section 3 corrected: the adjusted loss is 0.58x the pack, not double it [S4].

challenges.challenge: FY2026E FCFF of -Rp438.2bn is almost entirely a Rp331.6bn delta-NWC that arises only because the model switches definitions: history is pack:nwc of -Rp273.8bn (FY2025A) while forecast NWC is 35% x revenue = +Rp57.8bn. That is a definitional step, not the working-capital drag at the stated growth rate the house card requires. It accounts for about Rp167bn of the -Rp1,350.5bn EV (PV at the FY2026 discount factor), and it makes FY2025A FCFF -Rp801bn against actual OCF of -Rp210bn.
challenges.answer: NWC restated to trade working capital: 66.861 at end-2025 (F25) and -422.268 at end-2024 (F26), forecast at 44% of revenue on the same definition. Delta-NWC FY2026E falls to 2.69 and FCFF to -1.90, removing the 331.6 definitional step and its EV effect [S4].

challenges.challenge: The DCF carries a negative terminal value of -Rp1,463.5bn (-Rp571.6bn PV), a perpetuity in which the company destroys growing cash for ever. A going-concern DCF must be floored at the abandonment or liquidation value of the assets it would otherwise keep operating (PP&E book Rp330.6bn, 149 NIEs, the Bekasi site), or the horizon cut. Without a floor the negative perpetuity double-counts and the -Rp1,350.5bn EV is not a defensible number even where the equity answer remains zero.
challenges.answer: The negative perpetuity no longer drives the answer: weights are dcf_life 0.7 (EV 0.0, floored at abandonment in the year of peak cumulative PV) and dcf_fcff 0.3 (EV -73.4 with a negative terminal value). Liquidation cross-check: PP&E 336.6 against net debt 694.6, so the assets accrue to creditors [S4].

challenges.challenge: WACC 10.8% is below the 11-13% house band (VAL_COMPOUNDER section 2) and below every covered PHARMA peer (11.0-12.0%); applied to negative FCFF it enlarges the negative EV. Section 4 also says the relevant rate for the equity is the 17.3% COE, yet the model discounts at the WACC. The direction of this flaw is bearish, so it cannot be defended as caution.
challenges.answer: Unlevered beta raised to 0.75 lifts WACC to 11.13%, inside the 11-13% band, with COE 17.87%. The DCF discounts at the WACC and the text now says so; at the COE the enterprise value is lower still. Equity is zero at either rate [S4].

challenges.challenge: The bull case is under-built and internally inconsistent. The narrative says gross margin turns positive ahead of plan, but the shock only adds +3pp to a -10% base (bull GM -7%), so the branch returns zero like the other two and the 20% weight is inert. No scenario models the one event that could change the equity: the Danantara capital injection management was reported to be coordinating on 25 June 2026 (S2/S7 related list; the article itself is not in the registry).
challenges.answer: Bull restated to what the shocks produce: revenue +5pp and gross margin +3pp (to 13%), mirrored by the bear at -5pp and -3pp. The Danantara recapitalisation is not valued because no terms are published; the 25 June 2026 report appears only in S7 related list and the article could not be archived. All three branches value the equity at zero [S4][S7].

challenges.challenge: Upside evidence is not valued: H1-2026 gross profit +Rp7.9bn and EBITDA -Rp5.1bn on Rp79.0bn of sales (near breakeven with the 407-employee cut executed in September 2025), 149 NIEs, Rp330.6bn PP&E, and the 112% 2026 revenue target all get one sentence. The equity still comes out at zero because net debt is Rp718.4bn, not because the gross line never turns. The report should say that plainly and show the EBITDA the zero survives.
challenges.answer: Value-versus-recovery bridge added in section 4: H1-2026 EBITDA is negative, FY2026E EBITDA is 1.6, and the reverse DCF shows the last price needs perpetual EBITDA of 74.4 (F31), about half of revenue. Zero holds on H1-run-rate economics and on PP&E recovery, which still leaves creditors short [S0][S4].

challenges.challenge: The governance work is thinner than the house earnings-quality card requires. The report cites only the FY2025 unqualified opinion and the non-Big-Four auditor. The AR records that the FY2024 consolidated accounts were qualified (wajar dengan pengecualian, with a Basis for Qualified Opinion) and refers to the auditor emphasis-of-matter paragraph that the Board was asked to resolve (S4 p210-211); S2/S7 also carry the BPK finding of financial-management irregularities (20 May 2024). None appears, and no flag is classified manipulation vs optics.
challenges.answer: Sourced the FY2024 qualified opinion and emphasis of matter (S4 pp.210-211) and the BPK investigative finding referred to the Attorney General (S9). Classified BPK as manipulation-class until the criminal process resolves, the FY2024 qualification as optics-class because the audited FY2024 filing is a scanned PDF that could not be extracted to identify its basis, and the FY2025 unqualified non-Big-Four opinion as optics-class [S4][S9].

challenges.challenge: Cost of debt is understated, in the opposite direction to the rest of the model. The 4.5% assumption gives FY2026 interest of about Rp31bn, but Q1-2026 interest was Rp4.4bn and Q2-2026 Rp23.0bn - Rp27.4bn already in H1, a Rp92bn annualised run-rate on Rp722.8bn of debt (S0). Peer cost_of_debt is 5.7-15.0%. If the Q2 charge persists the FY2026 loss is about Rp50bn worse than modelled, and the shareholder loan is on non-commercial terms that bear on the no-new-bank-lines assumption.
challenges.answer: Cost of debt set to 7.7% from H1-2026 interest annualised on average debt, reconciled to note 26 (7% short-term facilities, 6.9% Type E, concessional long-term). The Q2 charge is treated as an accrual lump rather than a step-up because the contractual rates do not support it. Mid-peer in PHARMA [S0][S4].

challenges.challenge: The central sensitivity claim is arithmetically wrong and the reverse DCF is missing. EBIT = revenue x (gross margin - opex%), so a full turn of gross margin into positive territory (GM 0%) leaves EBIT at -40% to -62% of sales; the sign cannot change until gross margin exceeds the opex ratio. What the suspended Rp126 implies is never quantified: market cap Rp390.5bn plus net debt Rp718.4bn is an EV of about Rp1,109bn, which at 10.8%/3% requires about Rp84bn of perpetual EBITDA (about 55% of current revenue). The reverse DCF also uses net debt Rp694.6bn (FY2025) while the bridge uses Rp718.4bn.
challenges.answer: Breakeven gross margin is the 17% expense ratio; the sensitivity sentence is rewritten and the table now shows the floor across the range. Reverse DCF quantified at 74.4 of perpetual EBITDA (F31). One net-debt figure throughout: debt 700.3 (F27) less cash 5.7 (F28) equals 694.6, replacing the 718.4 current-liability basis [S0][S4].

challenges.challenge: Citation hygiene. The ITB/Danantara biodiversity collaboration signed in October 2026 [S2] appears only in S2 Berita Terkait headline list, not the article body (the October article is not in the registry). FY2022 revenue of Rp980.4bn is cited [S4] although the AR comparatives run only 2023-25 (S4 p16; the figure is S0). The claim that the company is under special monitoring has no source in S4 or S5. S5 is cited for the non-Big-Four auditor, which it does not discuss.
challenges.answer: Registered S8 (the October 2026 biodiversity MoU) and cite it as an exploration agreement with no volume or price commitment, not the S2 related headline. Removed the unsourced special-monitoring claim; the suspension is cited to S5 and S6. FY2022 revenue is cited to S0 and the auditor and governance items to S4 [S0][S4][S8].

challenges.challenge: The model is not benchmarked to the covered peer set. Cost_of_debt 4.5% is the lowest in PHARMA (DVLA 9.0, KAEF 6.9, KLBF 7.5, MERK 8.5, SIDO 15.0), terminal g 3.0% is below the 4.0-4.5% common peer rate, and terminal opex 40% is above KLBF, MERK and PYFA. Section 2 sentence about the industry deck used for the sector is uncited and no PHARMA deck is in the packet.
challenges.answer: Cost of debt 7.7% is mid-peer against the 5.7-15.0% PHARMA range; terminal growth 4.0% matches the common 4.0-4.5% peer rate; terminal opex 17% is the H1-2026 actual, below the FY2025 67.5%. The uncited industry-deck sentence is replaced by an explicit statement that no PHARMA deck is in the registry, only the macro deck [S0][S4].

challenges.challenge: The claim stack ahead of equity is not quantified. The Rp245.3bn shareholder loan (F16) is a claim senior to the 3,099.3m shares, the loan agreement carries covenants and a cumulative cap (S4 note 26), and the post-homologation obligations include 407 early-retirement packages (S4 p43) plus the DPR unresolved employee-rights complaint (11 Nov 2025). The report says a recapitalisation would dilute but gives no arithmetic, so the downside section understates how little of any recovery reaches the minority.
challenges.answer: Claims stack quantified in section 5: total shareholder loans 629.7 (F30), of which 245.3 is short-term and secured on land and buildings (F16); conversion at the Rp126 last price would issue 4,997.9m shares (F32) against 3,099.3m existing; the early-retirement and homologation obligations were paid in cash in FY2025. The DPR complaint could not be verified and is not asserted [S4].

challenges.challenge: QC Q1 (FIX) is still open and still in the text: Section 4 prints the market capitalisation as IDR390,507,705,000.0bn, six orders of magnitude too large (correct Rp390.5bn = 3,099.2675m shares x Rp126). That sentence is load-bearing for the whole positive-number-on-a-negative-equity-balance-sheet argument.
challenges.answer: Market capitalisation is now rendered in the pack IDR bn unit with the idrb format in both the investment summary and section 4: Rp390.5bn = 3,099.3m shares x Rp126. The central positive-number-on-negative-equity sentence therefore carries the intended order of magnitude [S0][S4]. QC Q1 is closed by the same change.

challenges.challenge: Section 4 states the price requires perpetual EBITDA of 74.4 IDR bn while the accepted C10 answer computed about Rp84bn on the same construction, and the amount renders as 74.4 IDR bn rather than in the pack money unit. With the net debt now used (Rp694.6bn) and market cap Rp390.5bn the implied EV is about Rp1,085bn, so the figure must be reproducible from the stated WACC and terminal growth.
challenges.answer: Recomputed from the figures the report now prints: EV = market cap 390.5 + net debt 694.6 = 1,085.1; 1,085.1 x (11.13% - 4.00%) / 1.04 = 74.4. This replaces the superseded 84bn figure computed at 10.8%/3%. The amount renders as IDR74.4bn via idrbn and the arithmetic is stated in words. One net-debt figure (694.6 at 31 Dec 2025) is used in sections 3 and 4 [S0][S4].

missing_bull_case.note: Under-built. H1-2026 is near EBITDA breakeven (EBIT -Rp5.4bn, gross profit +Rp7.9bn on Rp79.0bn sales), 149 NIEs and Rp330.6bn of PP&E survive, and a Danantara capital injection was reported under coordination on 25 Jun 2026; none is valued and the bull narrative (GM turns positive) is not implemented by its own +/-3pp shock, so the 20% bull branch is inert.

missing_bear_case.note: The report gives only the FY2025 unqualified opinion. It omits that FY2024 consolidated accounts were qualified (wajar dengan pengecualian, with a Basis for Qualified Opinion) and carry an emphasis-of-matter paragraph (S4 p210-211), the BPK finding of financial-management irregularities, and the severance/post-homologation claims (407 early retirements, S4 p43, DPR query 11 Nov 2025) that rank ahead of equity. None is quantified.

assumption_realism.note: The three value drivers are not consistent with the last actual. FY2026E gross margin is -10.0% against +10.0% actual in H1-2026; opex is 62% of sales against the pack 16.8% H1 line and 67.5% FY2025; net loss -Rp150.5bn implies an H2 loss 3.5x H1 of -Rp33.1bn. Revenue growth 9% against the company 112% plan is at least sourced (working capital).

evidence_and_citations.note: The FY2025A base year still uses pack EBIT (-Rp208.2bn, implied opex Rp189bn) although F5 restates opex to Rp94.857bn; no ebit fact was added, so the calibration artefact is in the model. The statement that the underlying loss is roughly double the pack is inverted (-Rp121.6bn vs -Rp208.2bn). S2 is cited for an Oct-2026 event via a related-link, FY2022 revenue is cited to S4 although the AR carries 2023-25 only, and special monitoring is unsourced.

valuation_method_fit.note: FY2026E FCFF of -Rp438.2bn is dominated by a Rp331.6bn delta-NWC that exists only because the NWC definition switches from pack (-Rp273.8bn) to 35% x revenue (+Rp57.8bn); FY2025A FCFF is -Rp801bn against actual OCF -Rp210bn. The terminal value is a -Rp1,463.5bn negative perpetuity with no abandonment floor, and the 10.8% WACC is below the 11-13% house band while the text says equity should carry the 17.3% COE. No quantified reverse DCF.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose claims the business loses money on every rupiah of sales when H1-2026 gross margin is +10%, and claims a positive gross margin is the only assumption that changes the sign when EBIT needs gross margin above the opex ratio (40-62%). The conclusion survives a doubled bear probability and a bull implementation, but the stated reasons overreach and the sensitivity claim is wrong.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: No PHARMA sector deck is in the packet and the section 2 deck sentence is uncited. Against the covered peer set (cov_publish comps) cost_of_debt 4.5% is the lowest (DVLA 9.0, KAEF 6.9, KLBF 7.5, MERK 8.5, SIDO 15.0), terminal g 3.0% is below the 4.0-4.5% common peer rate, and terminal opex 40% is above KLBF, MERK and PYFA. Each needs alignment or a source.

conservatism_audit.note: Unsourced departures below the last actual: gross margin -10% vs +10% H1-2026; opex 62% vs ~17% H1 pack line; terminal g 3.0% (judgment, no source). Revenue 9% vs the 112% plan is sourced (working capital). D&A 8% and capex 0.5% are LK-consistent; payout and tax at zero are defensible. The stack moves the DCF but not the floored target, which is the only reason it is not fatal on its own.

calibration.note: The gate is marked justified but the justification is false in the model: the FY2025A line remains pack EBIT, so the 65.4pp gap is self-created. A proper ebit fact (-Rp121.6bn excluding the Rp80.1bn other income) would cut the gap to roughly 8pp. The restatement is incomplete (selling expense is also excluded from the opex fact), so the gate cannot be relied on as passed.

signoff.notes: APPROVED SELL, target Rp0, price Rp126 (suspended). Round-2 sign-off: all 15 FATAL/MATERIAL challenges (C1-C13, L1, L2) answered and the fixes are in the model. Zero equity is robust to every residual QC item: net debt Rp720.6bn at 30 Sep 2026 vs FY2026E EBITDA Rp1.6bn; at 9M ratios EBITDA about Rp4.4bn, roughly Rp716bn short. Non-blocking, for the reader: post_bs_review and section 4 still anchor to 30 Jun 2026 and carry net debt Rp694.6bn (31 Dec 2025) not the pack Rp720.6bn / equity -Rp755.5bn; FY2026E revenue Rp158.1bn vs 9M actual Rp134.0bn implies Q4 Rp24.0bn vs Q3 Rp55.0bn, unsourced; 51.0 employees decimal and citation gaps. Freshness defects from the 9M pack arriving after the model build; none moves a target of zero. No konglo analogue to PEHA/KAEF - INAF holds no covered peer stake. PHARMA batch not uniformly tilted.

bias.note: Base case reproduces the restructured run-rate on both drivers: FY2026E GM 10.0 and opex 17.0 equal the H1-2026 actuals (79.04 revenue, 7.92 GP, 13.28 opex = 16.8%) [S0], and FY2026E EBIT -11.1 is the H1 EBIT -5.36 annualised (-10.7). The +73pp EBITDA-margin step is EBIT-neutral: opex falls from the FY2025 67.5 to 17.0 after the 413-to-51 cut and D&A is restated to the LK note 13 (12.07 vs the pack 1.1) [S4]. The pack's 9M-2026 actuals are slightly better than the anchors (GM 10.7, opex 15.2, Q3 GM 11.6), so the base is modestly conservative, not optimistic; at 9M ratios EBITDA would be about 4.4 vs the modelled 1.6, which is still 690 short of net debt, so the zero target is not moved by it. No unsourced optimism: terminal g 4.0 at the 4.0-4.5 peer rate, cost of debt 7.7 mid-peer, WACC 11.13 at the floor of the 11-13 band but argued from a 0.75 beta and COE 17.9 [S4]. Scenarios mirror the same two drivers (+/-5pp revenue, +/-3pp GM), base 50/30/20, and all three return zero because bull GM 13 is still below the 17 expense ratio [S0][S4].

recomputed.item: Perpetual EBITDA implied by the last price

findings.finding: post_bs_review is anchored to the 30 June 2026 balance sheet and section 4 says 'the June-2026 net debt is higher', but the pack the model was built on (asof 2026-11-14 15:37) now carries 30 September 2026: debt 731.9, cash 11.3, net debt 720.6, equity -755.5 [S0]. The freshest balance sheet is a quarter newer than the text says.

The base-case drivers are held at the H1-2026 ratios (GM 10.0, opex 17.0) while the pack now carries 9M-2026 actuals: GM 10.7 (Q3 11.6), opex 15.2 (Q3 13.0), 9M revenue 134.0 vs 9M-2025 133.7 [S0]. FY2026E revenue 158.07 implies Q4 of 24.0 against Q3's 55.0.
The duplicated fact units are fixed (126 mn units, no 'million units'); F15 headcount still renders '51.0 employees', a decimal on a headcount.

The summary's 'recorded no trading volume in any quarter of 2025 [S4][S5]' is evidenced by the pack's zero-volume fields (ADTV 0, 63 zero-volume days) [S0], not by the AR or the delisting article; and 'the June 2026 report ... is not in the registry [S2]' conflicts with section 5 and post_bs_review, which cite the registered headline [S7].
Section 6 gives the cash-conversion test (FY2025 OCF -210 vs net loss -78) but not the 3-year accruals ratio the earnings-quality card asks for on a non-financial.

The NWC justification calls the pack's nwc 'all current assets less all current liabilities'; it is non-cash current assets less non-debt current liabilities (verified: 119.23 - 5.69 - 632.65 + 245.28 = -273.83) [S0].

flags.message: FY+1 ebitda margin moves +73.2pp from FY2025A: source the change
flags.justification: The step is sourced to the H1-2026 actuals, not an upgrade on hope: the pack shows H1-2026 revenue of Rp79.0bn, gross profit of +Rp7.9bn (10.0% margin) and EBITDA of about -Rp5.1bn, after the headcount cut from 413 to 51 and the shift to toll manufacturing [S0][S4]. FY2025A is also restated to the LK's operating loss excluding the Rp80.1bn one-off other income, which lowers the base-year margin the gate compares against [S4].

flags.message: nwc FY2024A restated at 0.49x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The data pack's nwc is all current assets less all current liabilities, which nets tax payables, accruals and the pre-deconsolidation payables of the bankrupt distribution subsidiary; on the forecast definition (trade receivables plus inventories less trade payables) the LK balances give -Rp422.3bn at end-2024 and +Rp66.9bn at end-2025 [S4]. The restatement puts history on the same revenue-scaled definition the forecast uses.

flags.message: nwc FY2025A restated at -0.24x the data pack: say why the pack is wrong
flags.justification: The pack's -Rp273.8bn is a current-liabilities net figure, not revenue-scaled working capital; the LK shows trade receivables of Rp18.7bn plus inventories of Rp65.6bn less trade payables of Rp17.4bn, i.e. +Rp66.9bn or 44.1% of FY2025 revenue [S4]. Without the restatement the forecast books a Rp331.6bn definitional cash outflow in FY2026E that is not a working-capital movement.

flags.message: expected return -100%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers produce a zero equity value even on the H1-2026 run-rate: gross margin is 10% and opex 17%, leaving EBIT negative [S0]; net debt on the last audited balance sheet is Rp694.6bn against a DCF enterprise value that is at best zero on the abandonment floor [S4]; and the shareholder loan of Rp629.7bn is senior to the 3,099.3m shares [S4]. At the suspended Rp126 price the market cap of Rp390.5bn implies about Rp1,085bn of enterprise value, which no reverse DCF reproduces.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.6, 'pe': 0.3, 'ev_ebitda': 0.1}
flags.justification: P/E and EV/EBITDA are undefined on negative EBIT and negative EBITDA, so the PHARMA default weights cannot be used [S4]. We weight a life DCF floored at abandonment (70%) above the perpetuity FCFF DCF (30%) because the perpetuity carries a negative terminal value for a company that destroys cash at the margin; neither method reaches the net debt, so the equity is zero [S4].
